name: rail-steps-down-twice
prompt: A 3.3 V rail carries 2 A from a buck to a QFN-32 and to two 0402 bypass capacitors. The QFN pads are 0.36 mm across on a 0.65 mm pitch and it has an exposed thermal pad. There is a ground pour on the same layer with a keepout under the antenna. Fab is JLCPCB standard. Write the rules, the routes and the tags, build it, and prove the rules applied.

inputs.notes: Composition, not a single rule. The five older cases each isolate one behaviour and every one of them would pass against an agent that cannot compose a rule set. Here the rail wants a class width neither the QFN pad nor the 0402 terminal can accept, so two different step-down rungs are needed; the pour wants its own clearance, deliberately above trace-to-trace; and the thermal pad wants relief or direct connect. Those rules contend, and resolving them is the skill.
inputs.environment: Commands run from the repository root with an interpreter that has jitx and jitxlib.verify installed and a reachable runtime.

expected_output: A rule set, layout code carrying routes and tags, and checks, all three. The design builds and the checks assert on the captured design rather than on the authored input.

assertions.text: every declared rule is witnessed by a check the agent wrote, reported through rule_coverage with the unwitnessed count named
the trunk realizes at the class width, and each escape realizes strictly inside its own narrowest selected pad, asserted against the measured pad width directly and not only through a width tolerance
the two step-down rungs are distinct, because the QFN pad and the 0402 terminal do not accept the same escape width, and each outranks the class rule while losing to the pad-connection rule
clearance_relaxations is run and reports no rule relaxed, or names the relaxation and how it was resolved
the pour realizes with positive area and respects the keepout, measured rather than inferred from build status
no check passes on an empty selection: a gate that measured nothing fails
the checker library the skill routes to is importable in the environment used
